rounds.text: Daulat Securities Ltd trades at a steep discount to its underlying asset base, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.65x against a book value of ₹ 43.2 per share [E1], positioning the stock well below its book valuation compared to a sector benchmark of 1.31x [E6]. Operational top-line performance shows explosive expansion, highlighted by a compounded sales growth of 257% over the trailing twelve months [E13], supported by screen signals showing sales up 62% year-over-year [E44] and net profit surging by 73% year-over-year [E46]. Profitability metrics at the margin level demonstrate massive structural leverage, as operating margins reached 536% in the trailing twelve months compared to 75% three years earlier, marking a monumental 461 percentage point expansion [E23]. This impressive operational momentum is further reinforced by a recent quarterly operating margin of 89% in June 2026, which improved by 9 percentage points over the year-ago quarter [E24]. Balance sheet risk is virtually nonexistent since the company is almost debt free with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.00x and flat borrowings of ₹ 0.00 Cr [E30, E31, E38], while insider commitment strengthens as promoters increased their stake to 56.98% by September 2026 compared to 55.46% in December 2023 [E33]. Conceded: [E27, E28, E29, E42] operating cash flow is negative at ₹ -0.62 Cr with weak cash conversion of 0.35x and drastically expanded working capital days.

Conceded: [E13]. Despite robust top-line acceleration, profitability is fundamentally detached from sales expansion, with compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months resting at -1% [E14]. The underlying operational quality is heavily impaired, evidenced by a negative return on equity of -8.7% [E12], a negative return on capital employed of -9.6% [E11], and a dismal 10-year median ROE of just 4% [E19]. Furthermore, cash generation is deeply problematic; operating cash flow for March 2026 sits at negative Rs -0.62 Cr [E28] alongside free cash flow of negative Rs -0.67 Cr [E29], yielding a distressed cash conversion ratio of just 0.35x against reported profits [E27]. Working capital inefficiency has worsened severely, with working capital days doubling from 1,523 days to an alarming 3,040 days [E42]. Compounded share price performance reflects this chronic destruction of value, dragging the 1-year return down by -24% [E18] and leaving the stock languishing at a mere 25% of its 52-week range [E4].

Conceded: [E14], [E28], [E29], and [E42]. However, the bear's emphasis on historical weakness ignores a powerful operational turnaround that is actively invalidating stale sentiment [E49]. Compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months has surged by 257% [E13], supported by screen reasons highlighting strong sales growth of 62% YoY and net profit jumping 73% YoY [E44, E46]. Operating margins have expanded dramatically to 536% in the TTM from 75% three years earlier, a massive gain of 461 percentage points [E23], while quarterly operating margins reached 89% in June 2026 [E24]. Insider conviction is rising concurrently, with promoters increasing their holdings to 56.98% by September 2026 [E33]. Furthermore, the business operates with a pristine, debt-free balance sheet of 0.00x debt-to-equity [E30, E38] and trades at a steep discount of just 0.65x its book value [E1, E39], offering a deeply mispriced entry point for a rapidly accelerating enterprise.

Conceded: [E13], [E23], [E24], [E33], and [E38]. However, the bull's narrative of an operational turnaround is fundamentally undermined by a compounding profit growth rate of -1% [E14] and deeply negative returns, including a trailing return on capital employed of -4.64% versus a sector benchmark of 5.46% [E9] and a median return on equity of -9% over the last year [E22]. The dramatic top-line surge has completely failed to translate into actual cash generation, evidenced by negative operating cash flow of Rs -0.62 Cr [E28] and negative free cash flow of Rs -0.67 Cr [E29] for March 2026, alongside a cash conversion ratio of just 0.35x [E27]. Furthermore, the claim of a mispriced entry point ignores the alarming structural deterioration in working capital, where days have ballooned from 1,523 days to an astonishing 3,040 days [E42]. Finally, the stock trades at 25% of its 52-week range [E4] and carries a 0.00% dividend yield [E3], reflecting market skepticism that the bull's cited metrics represent sustainable value rather than fleeting accounting distortions.
